NDT training in Houma, LA: how it works

Short answer: Houma and Terrebonne Parish technicians take NDT theory online at their own pace on the Atlantis portal, where an ASNT NDT Level III answers their questions. Practical skills are rehearsed in the Practical NDT simulator and then built hands-on at the employer's yard or shop. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Houma. Certification comes from your employer under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, or from ASNT central exams.

Houma's inspection work is marine and offshore work. Shipyards along the Houma Navigation Canal build tugs, barges, liftboats and offshore supply vessels; fabrication yards turn out decks, modules and structural steel; and Port Fourchon, about an hour south down Bayou Lafourche, is the supply base for most deepwater activity in the Gulf of Mexico. A Houma technician is far more likely to be checking hull plate, deck welds or aluminum superstructure than refinery piping.

The training model fits a workforce that often works on a vessel schedule or a rotation. Theory is self-paced, so it fits around a hitch. Hands-on hours come from real inspection under a certified Level II or Level III at a Houma employer. The employer then examines and certifies you to its written practice.

Send us your Houma training request with the methods, levels and number of people involved. We reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Houma: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Shipyards and marine contractors in Terrebonne and Lafourche parishes mostly certify their technicians under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, with classification society and customer requirements layered on top. The steps are the same whichever yard you work for.

  1. Read the employer's written practice. It names the methods the yard uses and sets training, experience, examination and vision requirements for each level. If you are job-hunting, the SNT-TC-1A eligibility page explains typical entry rules.
  2. Finish the formal training hours for your method and level through the portal. Recommended minimums by method are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. Build documented experience doing the method on hull, deck and piping welds under a certified technician, recorded in a signed log.
  4. Sit the general exam, a written test of the method's theory, equipment and terms.
  5. Sit the specific exam on the yard's procedures and the acceptance standards its customers and the classification society impose.
  6. Sit the practical exam on welded specimens like the ones the yard produces, graded by or under a Level III.
  7. Pass an eye examination for near vision and color contrast as the written practice requires.
  8. Get certified by the employer, whose signature makes the certification valid for work at that company.
  9. Keep it current through recertification at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years.

If you would rather hold a credential that is independent of any yard, Atlantis prepares candidates for ASNT central certification: ASNT 9712 at Level I and II, and the ASNT NDT Level III examinations.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Houma technicians

The courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. Most people start at Level 1, add Level 2 once their hours allow, and only later consider Level III. The table shows how each method is used in the Houma marine economy.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Houma
VTVisual acuity, lighting, weld gauges, fit-up and visual acceptance criteriaEvery hull, deck and superstructure weld in new construction and repair
MTYoke and prod techniques, field direction, visible and fluorescent particlesFillet and butt welds on steel hulls, crane pedestals, padeyes and lifting points
PTCleaning, penetrant dwell, excess removal, developing and interpretationAluminum superstructures and crew boat hulls, stainless piping and non-magnetic fittings
UTCalibration, thickness gauging through coatings where the gauge allows, angle-beam weld examinationHull and deck plate thickness surveys on vessels in repair, full-penetration welds in new builds
PAUT and TOFDEncoded scanning, focal laws, data analysis and sizing for UT Level II techniciansHeavy structural welds on offshore units where the owner and class accept advanced UT
RTExposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital interpretationPiping and pressure-boundary welds aboard vessels and on fabricated modules
ETImpedance-plane displays, probe choice and surface crack techniquesCrack checks through paint on structural details and on rotating equipment components

Level III preparation in Houma is usually taken by a yard's quality lead or an inspection company's technical manager. It covers the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and practice in writing procedures and examinations that a classification surveyor or a customer auditor will read.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Houma

UT in Houma divides into two jobs. In repair yards it is mostly thickness gauging: surveying hull plate, deck plate, tanks and structural members for wastage so the owner and the surveyor can decide what to crop and renew. In new construction it is angle-beam examination of full-penetration welds to the yard's procedure and the classification society's rules. The UT training course teaches both, with attention to coated surfaces, curved plate, couplant and reporting readings on a vessel plan.

Day to day, though, the methods Houma yards use most are VT and MT on steel welds, with PT wherever aluminum or stainless is involved. A new technician in a Terrebonne Parish yard usually earns surface-method certifications first and adds UT once the yard needs more volumetric capacity. Start with VT training, MT training and PT training if that is your situation.

Where NDT technicians work around Houma

Shipbuilding on the Houma Navigation Canal. Bollinger Shipyards runs a large new-construction yard on the west bank of the canal, the former Gulf Island Fabrication shipyard it acquired, building ocean-going tugs, barges, liftboats, offshore support vessels and government vessels. Thoma-Sea Marine Constructors also builds vessels in the Houma area. Yards like these need technicians in VT, MT, UT and RT for hull, deck and piping welds.

Vessel repair and conversion. Repair yards across Terrebonne and Lafourche parishes keep the Gulf's supply boats, crew boats and liftboats working. That means thickness surveys, crack checks and weld inspection between charters, often to tight deadlines.

Port Fourchon and offshore support. Port Fourchon serves most of the deepwater Gulf, and the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port lies offshore of it. Equipment, lifting gear and containers moving through the port are inspected before they go offshore, and service companies based there need MT, UT and VT.

Offshore and structural fabrication. Fabricators in the Houma area build decks, modules, skids and structural steel to AWS D1.1 and API offshore structural practice, inspected visually and with MT and UT.

Pipelines. Coastal Louisiana is crossed by pipelines serving offshore production and onshore terminals. Construction and repair work calls for weld inspection to API 1104 and thickness surveys on corroded lines.

NDT schools and classes near Houma: what to compare

If you are looking for NDT classes near Houma, you will find a mix of classroom programs elsewhere in south Louisiana and online courses that pair self-paced theory with practical training at an employer. Neither is automatically better. The test is whether the training record will satisfy the written practice of the yard that certifies you.

  • Ask which standard the course follows and whether the completion record shows method, level and hours clearly.
  • Ask who the Level III behind the course is and in which methods that person is certified.
  • Ask how the hands-on component works and what kind of specimens you will see; welded steel plate and pipe matter most for marine work.
  • Ask whether the course prepares you for employer examinations, ASNT central examinations or both.
  • Ask what you can show a new employer if you move yards.

Our own answers: self-paced theory on the portal with Level III Q&A, rehearsal in the browser simulator, and hands-on practical work and examination in person at the employer's facility under its written practice. The published US fees for each course are in the table on this page; Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal. The training FAQ covers the rest.

Online NDT training in Louisiana

For crew members on boats or offshore rotations, online theory is often the only realistic way to study. The Atlantis portal lets Louisiana technicians work through modules whenever they have time and connectivity, and send questions to the Level III as they go. Nothing is scheduled, so a missed week does not mean a missed class.

Online theory still has to be matched by a practical. Louisiana yards certify only after supervised hands-on experience and a practical examination on real welds. For the rest of the state, see NDT training in Louisiana; the national picture is on NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Houma facility (employers)

When a Houma yard wins a vessel contract and has to qualify new hires quickly, the usual pattern is theory online for the whole group, then hands-on training and practical examinations in person at the yard on its own equipment and weld samples. The specific examination is built around the yard's procedures and the acceptance criteria in the contract and class rules, so what the crew is tested on matches what they will inspect.

Yards also need their certification files to survive a classification society or customer audit. Written practice development aligns your document with the methods you really use, and outsourced Level III consulting can review procedures, prepare and grade examinations, and check technician files. Group arrangements are explained on the corporate training page.

Radiography licensing in Louisiana

Radiography in Houma is regulated by the state rather than directly by the NRC, because Louisiana has an Agreement State program. The Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality licenses radiography sources and the companies that use them under the radiation protection rules in LAC 33, Part XV, and it recognizes the industrial radiographer certification that people operating sources must hold. Trainees work under a certified radiographer while they gain experience.

None of that is covered by an NDT method course. RT training teaches technique, image quality and interpretation for SNT-TC-1A certification; radiation safety training and state certification run through the employer's licensed program. A Houma radiographer generally needs both. Check current requirements with LDEQ before planning an RT career route.

Practice before your practical exam

Before your practical, rehearse in Practical NDT, the browser-based simulator. For marine work the welding workshop, the ultrasonic testing simulator and the visual testing simulator are the closest to what a Houma yard will ask of you. Simulator time builds familiarity; it is not logged experience and it does not stand in for the practical examination on real welds.

Check your written knowledge with the free practice tests, method by method.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Houma

How long does NDT training take in Houma?

The theory can be completed fairly quickly when studied steadily, but the supervised experience hours set out in your yard's written practice take longer. Those hours, not the course, usually set the timeline.

What does NDT training cost in Houma?

Each course has a published US fee shown in the table on this page. For a group at a Houma yard, use the contact form and we will reply within one business day.

Can I study NDT online while working offshore?

Yes. Theory is self-paced on the portal, so you can study between shifts or on days off. The practical has to be done in person at your employer.

Where is the nearest NDT school to Houma?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Houma or elsewhere on the bayou. Our theory is online and the hands-on part takes place at the employer's facility. Use the questions above to compare any school you are considering.

Which NDT method is most useful in a Houma shipyard?

VT and MT on steel welds, then PT for aluminum and stainless. UT follows for thickness surveys and full-penetration welds.

Are Houma shipyards hiring NDT technicians?

Yards and marine contractors around Houma hire inspectors as contracts are won, and repair work continues between new builds. Demand moves with vessel orders and offshore activity.

Does ABS accept SNT-TC-1A certification?

Classification societies generally look at the yard's qualification program and the requirements in their own rules. Many US yards certify to SNT-TC-1A-based written practices, but the yard's Level III confirms what class and the customer require for each project.

Will my certification follow me to another yard?

Employer certification ends when you leave. The next yard reviews your records and certifies you under its written practice. ASNT central certification stays with you.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Houma?

Yes. The Level III course is self-paced online with questions answered by the instructor.

Who is the instructor?

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, who has worked in NDT internationally for more than eleven years.
